issues.body: ScoreBudget::TopK sorts every input score, truncates to k, and only then calls collect_scores, which filters non-finite values. In descending total_cmp order, NaN and +inf can occupy the selected prefix. For example, TopK(1) over [NaN, 1.0] can return an empty map instead of retaining the finite 1.0 score. This violates the documented claims that non-finite scores are dropped and TopK retains the k highest-scoring nodes, and can silently remove entities that should receive injected ranking scores.
issues.fix_hint: Exclude non-finite entries before sorting/truncating (for example, build the ranked vector from enumerate().filter(|(_, score)| score.is_finite())), then truncate and collect. Add a TopK regression test containing NaN and infinities that asserts the map retains min(k, finite_count) highest finite scores and excludes all non-finite entries.
issues.title: TopK truncates before dropping non-finite scores

verdict.summary: The dictionary-id adapter and cross-crate composition tests are generally well scoped, but the TopK path applies its budget before removing non-finite scores. Because f64::total_cmp orders NaN and positive infinity ahead of ordinary finite values in descending order, invalid entries can consume the retained slots and then be discarded, causing valid highest-scoring entities to be omitted and producing fewer than k entries even when at least k finite scores exist. The existing non-finite test exercises only ScoreBudget::All, so it does not cover this load-bearing interaction.
